questions.question: Which of the following words is correctly spelt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Vitiate**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'Vitiate'** means to spoil or impair the quality, value, or efficiency of something; it can also mean to make something legally invalid or ineffective. (**बिगाड़ना**)
 
 
• **Example: **Strategic mistakes can **vitiate** the entire plan and lead to failure.
 
 
 
• **'Vitiate'** is correctly spelt and refers to the act of corrupting or making something faulty or defective. (**दूषित करना**)
 
 
• **Example: **A technical error in the filing process might **vitiate** the legal contract.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word **'Vitiate'** is the correctly spelt option among the given choices.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Vitiate**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their meanings and examples:

__
 
• **Veracity **(सत्यता): The quality of being true, accurate, or the habit of telling the truth.
 
 
• **Example: **The jury had serious doubts about the **veracity** of the witness's testimony.
 
 
 
• **Vermilion **(सिंदूरी रंग): A brilliant red color or a pigment made from mercury sulfide.
 
 
• **Example: **The traditional bride wore a mark of **vermilion** on her forehead.
 
 
 
• **Varmine** (अशुद्ध वर्तनी): This is an incorrect spelling. The correct word is **'Vermin'**, which refers to small animals or insects that are harmful to crops or carry disease. (**नुकसानदेह कीड़े-मकोड़े**)
 
 
• **Example: **The old warehouse was infested with **vermin** and had to be professionally cleaned.

questions.question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.
The healthcare workers were praised for their dedication, sacrifise, and relentless service during the pandemic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sacrifice**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **sacrifise** as written in the provided sentence is **orthographically incorrect**. The correct **English spelling** is **sacrifice**, which uses the letter **c** instead of **s** in the third syllable.
 
• The term is defined as the act of giving up something highly valued for the sake of something else considered more important or worthy. In the context of the sentence, it refers to the **selfless acts** of **healthcare workers**.
 
• Etymologically, the word is derived from the Old French **sacrifise** (though modern French uses **sacrifice**) and the Latin **sacrificium**. The Latin root consists of **sacer** (holy) and **facere** (to make).
 
• The spelling error occurs due to **phonetic confusion**, as the letter **c** followed by **i** or **e** produces a soft **/s/** sound, leading writers to mistakenly substitute it with the letter **s**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Review of other terms in the sentence:
 
 
• **Dedication**: This is a correctly spelled noun referring to the quality of being committed to a task or purpose. It originates from the Latin **dedicare**, meaning to proclaim or devote.
 
• **Relentless**: This adjective is spelled correctly and signifies something that is **harsh**, **inflexible**, or **unceasing**. It is a combination of the word **relent** and the suffix **-less**.
 
• **Pandemic**: A correctly spelled noun/adjective describing an outbreak of a disease that occurs over a wide geographic area. It stems from the Greek **pan** (all) and **demos** (people), relating to its **global scale** impact.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Have the doctors administered the vaccine to all patients?

options.text: Were the vaccine administered to all patients by the doctors?
Have the vaccine been administered to all patients by the doctors?
Has the vaccine been administered to all patients by the doctors?
The vaccine has been administered to all patients by the doctors?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Has the vaccine been administered to all patients by the doctors?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense** and follows the **Interrogative** structure: **Have/Has + Subject + V3 + Object?**

• In the conversion to **Passive Voice**, the **Object** of the active sentence (**the vaccine**) becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence.

• Because **the vaccine** is a **Singular Noun**, the auxiliary verb must change from 'Have' to **Has** to ensure proper **Subject-Verb Agreement**.

• The passive form of the **Present Perfect** requires the inclusion of the auxiliary verb **been** placed between the new subject and the **Past Participle (V3)** form of the verb (**administered**).

• The agent or original subject (**the doctors**) is introduced at the end of the sentence using the preposition **by**.

• The final structure for the **Passive Interrogative** becomes: **Has + New Subject (the vaccine) + been + V3 (administered) + by + Agent?**

 **Additional Information__**

• **Subject-Verb Agreement**:

• The word **Have** is used with plural subjects or the pronouns I, you, we, and they.

• The word **Has** is strictly used with **third-person singular** subjects like 'the vaccine'.

• **Tense Preservation**:

• Using **Were** would incorrectly change the tense to **Simple Past**.

• The construction must remain in the **Present Perfect** to maintain the original meaning.

• **Sentence Type**:

• An interrogative sentence must retain its **Question** format by placing the auxiliary verb before the subject.

• Changing the order to 'The vaccine has been...' transforms it into an **Assertive** sentence, which is grammatically incorrect for this conversion.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Were the monks chanting prayers in the monastery?

options.text: Were prayers being chanted by the monks in the monastery?
Were prayers chanted by the monks in the monastery?
Had prayers been chanted by the monks in the monastery?
Are prayers being chanted by the monks in the monastery?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Were prayers being chanted by the monks in the monastery?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is an **Interrogative Sentence** in the **Past Continuous Tense**. The active voice structure for this tense is: **Was/Were + Subject + Verb (ing form) + Object?**

• To convert a **Past Continuous** interrogative sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure used is: **Was/Were + Object (New Subject) + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject (New Object)?**

• In the active sentence, **the monks** is the **Subject**, **chanting** is the **Verb**, and **prayers** is the **Object**.

• When converting to passive, the plural object **prayers** becomes the new subject. Since it is plural, the auxiliary verb **Were** is retained at the beginning of the sentence.

• The verb **chanting** is transformed into **being chanted** to maintain the continuous aspect in the passive form.

• The original subject **the monks** is placed after the preposition **by**. The prepositional phrase **in the monastery** remains at the end to provide context.

 **Additional Information__**

• Understanding the construction of other tenses helps in identifying the incorrect options:

• **Simple Past Passive**: Uses the structure **Was/Were + V3**. This is why 'Were prayers chanted...' is incorrect as it lacks the continuous marker **being**.

• **Past Perfect Passive**: Uses the structure **Had + been + V3**. This changes the timeline of the action from 'ongoing in the past' to 'completed before another past action'.

• **Present Continuous Passive**: Uses **Is/Am/Are + being + V3**. This is incorrect because the original sentence is set in the **Past Tense**, and the tense must remain consistent during voice conversion.

• **Voice Change Principle**: In English grammar, while the **Voice** (Active to Passive) changes, the **Tense** of the sentence must remain the same. The focus simply shifts from the doer of the action to the receiver of the action.

</ul

• In English grammar, the noun **'attempt'** is commonly followed by the preposition **'at'** when referring to an effort made to achieve a specific **target**, **goal**, or **record**. 
• The phrase **'attempt at something'** or **'attempt at doing something'** is a standard idiomatic collocation used to describe trying to accomplish a feat. 
• In this context, **Deepak** is trying to break or reach the **world record**, so **'at'** is the most appropriate preposition to link the attempt to the objective. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. **Complete Sentence:** *'Deepak made several attempts **at**__ the world record in the long jump, but in vain.'* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: 'for'** is often used with the verb **'strive'** or **'aim'**, but for the noun **'attempt'** in the context of a record, **'at'** is preferred. 
• **Option 3: 'in'** is typically used for locations or time periods and does not fit the target-oriented nature of the sentence. 
• **Option 4: 'about'** is used to indicate a subject or theme, which is incorrect in this grammatical structure. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
Despite repeated reminders from the court, the authorities continued to drag their foot on implementing the order.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**drag their feet**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined phrase **drag their foot** is an incorrect variation of the established **English idiom** **drag one's feet**.
 
• The idiom **drag one's feet** (or **drag their feet**) means to act with **reluctance** or to **deliberately delay** a process because one does not want to do it.
 
• In the context of the sentence, the **authorities** are stalling the implementation of a **court order**, which fits the figurative meaning of **avoiding or postponing action**.
 
• Linguistically, **idioms** are fixed expressions; the plural noun **feet** is a mandatory component of this specific phrase, making the singular **foot** grammatically unacceptable in this context.
 
• Options such as **drag in their foot** or **drag with their feet** are incorrect because they introduce **superfluous prepositions** that are not part of the standard **idiomatic structure**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Idiomatic Consistency**:
 
 
• Fixed expressions like **drag one's feet** do not follow standard **compositional rules**, meaning their parts cannot be substituted for synonyms or different grammatical numbers without losing the intended meaning.
 
• The term **foot-dragging** is a derived noun used in **political and legal discourse** to describe **prevarication** or **intentional obstruction**.
 
 
 
• **Synonymous Expressions**:
 
 
• **Stonewall**: To refuse to provide information or help, especially to **delay progress**.
 
• **Procrastinate**: To keep **delaying** something that must be done, often out of laziness or reluctance.
 
• **Dilly-dally**: To waste time through **indecision** or aimless action.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
Three-fourth of the cake has been eaten by the guests, and the remaining portion will be served to the kitchen staff later.

options.text: Three-fourth of the cake have been eaten
Three-fourths of the cake has been eaten
Three-fourths of the cake have been eaten

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three-fourths of the cake has been eaten**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Pluralization of Fractions**: In English grammar, when a fraction has a **numerator** greater than 1 (such as 2, 3, or 5), the **denominator** must be in its plural form. Therefore, while we say **one-fourth**, we must say **three-fourths**.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement with Fractions**: When a fraction is followed by the preposition **of**, the **verb** agrees with the noun that follows the preposition. If the noun is **singular** or **uncountable**, a **singular verb** is used. If the noun is **plural**, a **plural verb** is used.

• **Analysis of the Noun**: In this sentence, the noun following the fraction is **cake**, which is **singular**. Therefore, the auxiliary verb must also be **singular**. The singular auxiliary verb **has** is the correct choice to accompany **cake**.

• **Grammatical Consolidation**: The original sentence used **Three-fourth**, which lacks the necessary plural suffix **-s** for the denominator. The correct improvement must include both the pluralized denominator and the singular verb **has**.

• Therefore, the option **Three-fourths of the cake has been eaten** is the correct one.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Countable vs. Uncountable Contexts**:

• If the sentence referred to multiple separate cakes, such as **three-fourths of the cakes**, the verb would change to **have** to maintain agreement with the plural noun.

• The word **cake** in this context refers to a single whole item being partitioned, thus necessitating **has**.

• **Hyphenation Rules**:

• While the provided answer does not use a hyphen, it is common in formal writing to hyphenate fractions when they function as **adjectives** (e.g., a **three-fourths** share). When acting as a **noun**, the hyphen is often omitted, though usage varies between style guides.

• **Fractional Proportions**:

• This rule applies to all proportions, including **percentages**. For example, **fifty percent of the cake has** been eaten, but **fifty percent of the guests have** arrived.

</ul

questions.question:
Identify the error in the sentence:
"He will comes to the office next week."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary grammatical error in the sentence is the use of the verb form **comes** after the modal verb **will**.
 
• In English grammar, **modal auxiliary verbs** (such as **will**, **shall**, **can**, **could**, **must**, **may**, and **might**) are always followed by the **base form** (infinitive without 'to') of the main verb.
 
• The word **comes** is the third-person singular present form. To correct the sentence, it must be replaced with the base form **come**.
 
• Thus, the error lies in the word **comes**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **comes**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'He **will come** to the office next week.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Will**: This is a modal verb used to indicate the **future tense**. It does not change its form regardless of the subject (I, you, he, she, they).
 
• **To the office**: This is a **prepositional phrase** acting as an adverb of place, indicating the destination. It is grammatically correct.
 
• **Next week**: This is a **time expression** used to denote a point in the future, which is consistent with the use of the future tense helper **will**.
</ul

questions.question:
Identify the error:

"I prefer reading than watching TV in evenings."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the use of the word **than**.
 
• The verb **prefer** is used to indicate a liking for one thing over another and is traditionally followed by the preposition **to** when comparing two nouns or gerunds.
 
• The standard grammatical structure is **prefer [something] to [something else]**.
 
• In the given sentence, the comparison is between two gerunds (**reading** and **watching**), so the word **than** must be replaced with **to**.
 
• Therefore, the word **than** is the incorrect part of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **than**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'I prefer reading **to** watching TV in evenings.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **than**: This is a conjunction used to introduce the second element in a comparison, typically following comparative adjectives like **better**, **faster**, or **more**.
 
• **prefer**: Apart from **to**, **prefer** can also be followed by a **to-infinitive** or the phrase **rather than** (e.g., 'I prefer to read **rather than** watch TV'). However, when gerunds are used, **to** is the standard preposition.
 
• Other words that take **to** instead of **than** for comparison include **senior**, **junior**, **superior**, **inferior**, and **prior**.
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate one-word substitute.

A person who looks on while others are doing something, without participating, is called a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Spectator**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The description **'A person who looks on while others are doing something, without participating'** refers to an **observer**. (पर्यवेक्षक)
 
 
• **Example: **The **independent observer** watched the **election process** to ensure it was conducted fairly.
 
 
 
• **'Spectator'** refers to a person who **watches** an event, **show**, or **sports match** without taking part in it; they are present only to view the **activity**. (दर्शक)
 
 
• **Example: **Thousands of **spectators** gathered at the **stadium** to watch the **Olympic** opening ceremony.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate **one-word substitute** for the given phrase is **'spectator'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **Spectator**

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Helper **(सहायक): A person who **assists** or **aids** another person in performing a task.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite. 

P. It reflects sunlight and shines at night. 

Q. The Moon controls the ocean tides on Earth. 

R. It moves around the Earth in about 27 days. 

S. The Moon has different shapes called phases. 

6. It helps scientists study space and Earth's movement.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The passage provides a structured introduction to the **Moon**, starting from its definition to its visual characteristics, its motion, and finally its influence on Earth and science.
 
• **Sentence 1** introduces the **Moon** as the Earth's only **natural satellite**, establishing the primary subject.
 
• **Sentence P** logically follows by describing the **Moon's** most noticeable property: it **reflects sunlight** and **shines at night**.
 
• **Sentence R** introduces the orbital behavior of the satellite, noting that it **moves around the Earth** in approximately **27 days**.
 
• **Sentence S** connects the previous points; the combination of the **Moon's** **position in its orbit** (R) and its **reflection of sunlight** (P) results in the changing shapes we see, known as **phases**.
 
• **Sentence Q** describes the **gravitational influence** of the **Moon**, specifically how it **controls the ocean tides** on **Earth**.
 
• **Sentence 6** concludes the passage by linking these physical effects and movements to their utility for **scientists** in studying **space** and **Earth's movement**.
 
• The most logical sequence that maintains this scientific and observational flow is **PRSQ**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'The **Moon** is the Earth's only **natural satellite**. It **reflects sunlight** and **shines at night**. It **moves around the Earth** in about **27 days**. The **Moon** has different shapes called **phases**. The **Moon** controls the **ocean tides** on Earth. It helps **scientists** study **space** and **Earth's movement**.'</div

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. A sniffer dog is trained to detect smells. 

P. The dog learns to identify harmful or hidden items. 

Q. It works at airports, stations, and public places. 

R. The dog alerts officers when it finds danger. 

S. It starts training when it is very young. 

6. Sniffer dogs help keep people safe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes the lifecycle and role of a **sniffer dog**, beginning with its training and ending with its contribution to public safety. 
• **Sentence 1** introduces the subject: 
• 'A **sniffer dog** is trained to **detect smells**.' 
• **Sentence S follows** Sentence 1 as it provides chronological detail about the **training** mentioned in the introduction: 
• 'It **starts training** when it is **very young**.' 
• **Sentence P is the second part** of the sequence because it elaborates on what the dog specifically **learns** during that early training phase: 
• 'The dog **learns to identify** **harmful or hidden items**.' 
• **Sentence Q follows** as it moves from the training phase to the **operational phase**, describing where the dog is deployed: 
• 'It **works** at **airports**, **stations**, and **public places**.' 
• **Sentence R is the final part** of the sequence as it describes the specific **action** the dog takes while on duty when it encounters a threat: 
• 'The dog **alerts officers** when it **finds danger**.' 
• The paragraph concludes with **Sentence 6**, which summarizes the outcome: 'Sniffer dogs help **keep people safe**.' 
• The correct sequence is **SPQR**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'A **sniffer dog** is trained to **detect smells**. It **starts training** when it is **very young**. The dog **learns to identify** **harmful or hidden items**. It **works** at **airports**, **stations**, and **public places**. The dog **alerts officers** when it **finds danger**. Sniffer dogs help **keep people safe**.'</div
